artists.biography:
Steven John Wilson (born 3 November 1967) is an English musician, best known as the founder, lead guitarist, singer and songwriter of progressive rock band Porcupine Tree. He is involved in many other bands and musical projects both as musician and producer (including No-Man and Blackfield) and also maintains a solo career.
Wilson is a self-taught producer, audio engineer, guitar and keyboard player, playing other instruments as and where required (including bass guitar, concert harp, hammered dulcimer and flute).
He used to split his living time between Tel Aviv and London, England, but he no longer holds a permanent residence in Tel Aviv.

perplexity.description:
The Raven That Refused to Sing (And Other Stories) is the third solo album by British musician Steven Wilson, originally released on February 25, 2013, by Kscope Music Records and Transmission Recordings. The album is firmly rooted in progressive rock, featuring a blend of intricate musicianship and atmospheric storytelling. It consists of six tracks, three of which are extended epics exceeding ten minutes, each inspired by supernatural tales. The music combines Wilson’s signature melancholic melodies with complex arrangements, supported by a stellar lineup including guitarist Guthrie Govan, bassist Nick Beggs, drummer Marco Minnemann, and saxophonist Theo Travis. The album was engineered by Alan Parsons, known for his work on Pink Floyd’s The Dark Side of the Moon.

This album holds a significant place in Wilson’s discography as a mature and cohesive work that showcases his skills as a composer and producer. It received critical acclaim for its emotional depth and technical proficiency, earning the Album of the Year award at the 2013 Progressive Music Awards. Critics praised it as a highlight of modern progressive rock, with The Guardian awarding it a 5/5 rating and calling Wilson “one of modern rock’s most cunning and soulful protagonists.” Commercially, it sold over 100,000 copies, reflecting both critical and fan appreciation.
